description: Assesses the appropriate observability and operational monitoring strategy based on service type, availability requirements, team capability, and deployment model.

recommendation.pattern: Full Observability Stack with SLO Monitoring
recommendation.rationale: Public-facing services with high availability targets require comprehensive observability including metrics, logs, traces, and Service Level Objective (SLO) monitoring. This enables rapid incident detection, root cause analysis, and proactive capacity management to maintain availability targets.

operationalBurden.staffingImplications: Requires SRE or platform engineering capability; on-call rotation for high-availability services
operationalBurden.ongoingMaintenance: Dashboard maintenance, alert tuning (reduce noise), SLO review, capacity forecasting, and runbook updates

costConsiderations.runningCosts: Significant for high-volume services; log ingestion and retention are primary cost drivers
costConsiderations.transitionCosts: Instrumentation effort; dashboard development; alert configuration; on-call process setup

recommendation.rationale: Containerised and cloud-native deployments with experienced teams benefit from OpenTelemetry-based observability. This provides vendor-neutral instrumentation that can export to multiple backends, avoiding lock-in while providing comprehensive metrics, logs, and traces.

operationalBurden.staffingImplications: Requires platform engineering skills; OpenTelemetry configuration needs initial investment but reduces long-term vendor dependency
operationalBurden.ongoingMaintenance: Collector configuration updates, dashboard maintenance, storage management, and instrumentation library updates

costConsiderations.runningCosts: Depends on backend choice; self-managed is cheaper but more operational effort; managed services are simpler but costlier
costConsiderations.transitionCosts: Application instrumentation; collector deployment; backend setup; dashboard development

recommendation.rationale: Internal services with teams that have limited cloud experience benefit from fully managed monitoring services with pre-built dashboards and automated alerting. This provides visibility without requiring deep observability engineering skills.

operationalBurden.staffingImplications: Standard development team can use pre-built dashboards; minimal configuration required
operationalBurden.ongoingMaintenance: Alert threshold tuning and periodic dashboard review

costConsiderations.runningCosts: Low to moderate; cloud-native monitoring often included in service pricing
costConsiderations.transitionCosts: Minimal; enable monitoring features and configure basic alerts

recommendation.rationale: Batch processing workloads require monitoring focused on job completion, processing duration, error rates, and data quality metrics rather than real-time request monitoring. Alerting should focus on job failures, SLA breaches, and data anomalies.

operationalBurden.staffingImplications: Development team manages job monitoring; no dedicated operations team needed
operationalBurden.ongoingMaintenance: Alert threshold updates, SLA monitoring configuration, and periodic review of job performance trends

costConsiderations.runningCosts: Low; custom metrics and basic alerting
costConsiderations.transitionCosts: Custom metric instrumentation; alert configuration; dashboard setup

recommendation.rationale: Without cloud access, observability requires self-managed monitoring infrastructure. Open-source tools like Prometheus, Grafana, and the ELK stack provide comprehensive monitoring but require dedicated infrastructure and administration.

operationalBurden.staffingImplications: Requires dedicated monitoring infrastructure management; Elasticsearch clusters need significant attention
operationalBurden.ongoingMaintenance: Infrastructure scaling, index management, retention policies, cluster health, and tool upgrades

costConsiderations.runningCosts: Hardware for monitoring infrastructure; staffing for administration; storage for logs and metrics
costConsiderations.transitionCosts: Infrastructure setup; tool installation and configuration; dashboard development

defaultRecommendation.rationale: When no specific conditions strongly favour an alternative, cloud-native monitoring services provide good visibility with minimal setup. These services offer metrics, logs, and basic alerting out of the box for most cloud resources.

costConsiderations.runningCosts: Low; included with most cloud services

commonQuestions: What are the key metrics that indicate service health?
Who will respond to alerts and what is the on-call model?
What is the log retention requirement for compliance?
Is there an existing monitoring platform to integrate with?
What SLOs need to be tracked?
Is distributed tracing needed for debugging?
evidenceNeeded: Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and key performance indicators
artefactsToProduce: SLO definitions and error budget policy
